_about: The deep active vision models of the timeline slide, each read in its paper. date: first public release (arXiv v1). name: the model's name. cite: authors, venue and venue year. row: where the label sits, -3, -2 and -1 above the axis, 1, 2 and 3 below, chosen so that labels do not overlap. seq-JEPA (arXiv:2505.03176 v1 2025-05-06, NeurIPS 2025, OpenReview GKt3VRaCU1, read 2026-10-29): learns without labels from sequences of views, each paired with the action leading to the next, predicting the next view's representation; its saccade experiments sample fixations from DeepGaze IIE saliency with inhibition of return, on STL-10; inspired by primate vision but compared with no brain or behavioral data, so among the models, not neuro_ai. Selection: each entry precise and distinctive; STAM (CVPR 2022) was dropped: the CanViT paper does not cite it and never seeing the whole image is not what sets it apart (RAM's glimpses do not cover it either). neuro_ai: active-vision models built to compare with brain or behavioral data, drawn on their own click; read on their abstract pages (2026-10-23): GVSM, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.06.06.658387, posted 2025-06-10: visual search from pixels in natural scenes, compared with human scanpaths and primate fronto-parietal activity; GPN, arXiv:2511.12715 v1 2025-11-16: predicts the next glimpse's embedding along human-like scanpaths, compared with human fMRI. How each obtains its viewpoints is not stated in the abstracts and is not claimed here. neuro_ai entries are drawn like the models, name and citation on a leader, at their row. pioneer: true for the model the field traces back to (the paper's Related work: "This line of research traces back to the Recurrent Attention Model"), highlighted on the slide.
